title: Service account onboarding and approval workflow for RBAC v2
creator: Samira Patel
description: Design and implement an end-to-end onboarding and approval flow for service accounts under RBAC v2. The goal is to make service account creation auditable, discoverable, and constrained to least-privilege defaults via templates, while integrating with SSO/SAML principal mapping and our audit logging pipeline. This ticket covers API/CLI endpoints, an admin approval step (optional for low-risk templates), naming/convention enforcement, automatic ownership assignments, and UI affordances for admins and owners.
acceptance_criteria: API/CLI endpoint exists to request a new service account with template selection
Admin approval workflow implemented and configurable per-template (auto-approve for low-risk templates)
Service account metadata includes owner, creation rationale, and audit log entry for every lifecycle event
SSO/SAML mapping doc and a working PoC that maps IdP groups to service account role bindings
Least-privilege templates stored in config with versioning and visible diff history
UI surfaces for admins to review pending requests, reassign ownership, revoke keys, and view audit trails
technical_notes: Create new endpoint POST /v1/service-accounts/requests that takes: name, template_id, justification, owner (optional), ttl (optional)
Requests create a pending object in DB and emit audit event 'service_account.request.created' to event pipeline
Admin approval implemented as a simple state machine: pending -> approved/rejected -> provisioned/archived
Provisioning step calls existing SA provisioning worker; include idempotency key and backoff on infra errors
Integrate SAML group claim mapping into RBAC v2 binding generator; mapping table stored in vault-backed config
Least-privilege templates include: permissions list, allowed resource scope, default TTL for keys, auto-approval flag
UI: new Admin > Service accounts > Requests view with filters (age, template, owner) and bulk-approve capability
Audit logging: every transition (request, approve, provision, key-rotate, revoke) must emit structured JSON to /audit stream with actor, reason, ip, session_id
Migration: surface existing service accounts in discovery job and mark owner if none, then create follow-up ticket to reconcile
Security: require MFA for admin approvals; mark templates that can bypass approval as 'low-risk' and record justification
